title: AlphaProof & AlphaGeometry 2 Achieve IMO Silver-Medal Formal Proving
whyItMatters: First AI system to achieve medal-level performance at the International Mathematical Olympiad with machine-verified Lean 4 proofs—igniting the RL + Lean formal math era.
summary: Google DeepMind paired a Gemini-based reinforcement-learning formal prover (AlphaProof) with a neuro-symbolic geometry engine (AlphaGeometry 2) to solve four of six problems at IMO 2024 (28/42 points, one point shy of gold), including the competition's hardest problem (P6), solved by only 5 of 609 human contestants. Every AlphaProof solution was formally checked in Lean, establishing the blueprint for combining LLMs, RL, and interactive theorem provers.
technicalHighlights: Solved IMO 2024 Problem 6—an ultra-hard number theory problem solved by <1% of top human olympians—with a Lean-checked proof.
Trained via AlphaZero-style test-time reinforcement learning over millions of auto-formalized mathematical statements.
Directly inspired the 2025–2026 wave of Lean-verified research math and software verification systems.
caveats: Required human experts to manually formalize problem statements into Lean beforehand and used up to three days of compute on the hardest problem.

scoreRationale.foundational: Proved reinforcement learning coupled with a formal proof verifier can discover non-trivial, creative multi-step proofs.
scoreRationale.ripple: Directly birthed the Lean + RL paradigm behind AlphaProof Code and the 2026 Millennium Problem formalizations.
scoreRationale.verification: Machine-verified in Lean 4 and graded by Fields Medalist Timothy Gowers and IMO coordinator Joseph Myers.
scoreRationale.velocity: Surpassed expectations for formal theorem proving years ahead of community forecasts.

sources.label: Google DeepMind: AI achieves silver-medal standard solving IMO problems
